full_query: Do fissures and hemmroids heal on their own?
sentences: Anal fissures and hemorrhoids have different healing outcomes depending on the severity and treatment methods employed

Acute Anal Fissures: These can often heal on their own with conservative management, which includes dietary modification (high-fiber diet), adequate hydration, and stool softeners to reduce strain during defecation
Chronic Anal Fissures: These are less likely to heal without medical intervention

Chronic fissures may require treatments such as topical nitrates, calcium channel blockers, or surgical options like lateral internal sphincterotomy, which has a high success rate for healing chronic fissures
Internal Hemorrhoids: Mild cases can resolve on their own with conservative measures like high-fiber diet, increased fluid intake, and over-the-counter treatments (e.g., topical agents, sitz baths)
Severe cases (grade III and IV) often require procedural interventions such as rubber band ligation, sclerotherapy, or surgical hemorrhoidectomy
External Hemorrhoids: These can also often resolve on their own, especially if they are not thrombosed
Conservative measures similar to those for internal hemorrhoids are recommended
Thrombosed external hemorrhoids can be very painful and may require medical procedures for relief
